result.summary: Supplies fresh randomness via GetRandHash() instead of all zeros as the BIP340 auxiliary data parameter when creating Schnorr signatures in MutableTransactionSignatureCreator. Adapts bip341_keypath_test_vectors to assert non-deterministic but valid signatures, and seeds the RNG in the script_sign fuzz target.
result.problem: Taproot Schnorr signatures are generated with static all-zero auxiliary data, leaving signing operations without the defense-in-depth side-channel and fault-injection resistance recommended by BIP340.
evidence: BIP340 specification recommends fresh randomness in auxiliary data to harden nonce generation against side channels and fault injection (quoted in description and commit message).
Fixes open issue #31883 ('SignatureCreator should supply auxiliary data argument for additional bip340 signature security').
result.scope_notes: Diff is small (+24/-5) across signing, test, and fuzzing code. Makes Schnorr transaction signing non-deterministic.
result.card: Bitcoin Core currently passes all-zero auxiliary data when signing Taproot inputs. This PR changes MutableTransactionSignatureCreator to pass fresh randomness from GetRandHash(), adhering to the BIP340 recommendation to protect against side-channel attacks and fault injection during signature generation. It also updates BIP341 keypath unit tests to handle non-deterministic signatures and seeds the RNG in script_sign fuzzing. This resolves issue #31883.

risk.why: A flaw in signature generation or RNG interaction during Schnorr signing could produce invalid signatures or crash transaction signing.
